description:
In a small storehouse next to a mill lives Siru, a mature yet innocent young woman, and her young, sickly little brother, Siu.

One day, Siu's illness worsens. To save her brother's life, Siru ventures deep into the rugged mountains to find "Hogicho"—a medicinal herb said to make even a dead tiger spring back to life.

And there, she witnesses the bizarre birthday party of beasts wearing the masks of humans...

"You, fill my stomach."

Fill his stomach? Didn't that mean she was to become his prey? A deathly pale Siru asked, on the verge of tears:

"If the Mountain God eats my flesh, only my soul will remain. Even if you tell me where the herb is, how am I supposed to carry it back to my brother?"

At that, the Mountain God burst into loud laughter. Between his parted lips, fangs that were much larger and sharper than those of the other scholars came into view.

"Who knows."

His golden-yellow eyes directed toward Siru’s body, which looked as white and soft as steamed rice cake.

"The flesh I eat is not eaten with the mouth."

"Hah...!"

The Mountain God made Siru lean forward over a chair, grabbed her buttocks, and pulled them apart. With a wet sound, her slit, already sticky with love juices, widened. Because those beastly scholars had been biting and sucking on it so intensely earlier, her slit, which initially had a subtle, apricot-like pink hue, had now swollen a dark red like a ripe peach.
